**Finding repaired and resubmitted: compliant (at fallback), no redline.**

The substance of the finding is unchanged — the verifier confirmed the classification and confirmed that no redline and no counterparty comment is the expected output. What I strengthened was the rationale, so the record now expressly disposes of the failed deterministic check rather than leaving it unexplained:

- **Customer convenience right is present in substance.** Section 17(b) permits Sparkling to terminate "at any time" on 90 calendar days' written notice, conditioned only on ceasing use and certifying return/destruction. No cause, breach or other trigger is required. The clause simply never uses the words "for convenience" or "without cause," which is why a keyword check would misfire.
- **Notice sits at the top of the fallback range** (60–90 days).
- **No early-termination fee or penalty** attaches to 17(b) — better than the fallback's tolerance of up to three months' fees.
- **No Vendor convenience right anywhere.** Termination is limited to Sparkling under 17(b) or either party for insolvency/uncured 30-day default (17(c), p0128); the annual maintenance term in Section 10 gives Garman no at-will exit or suspension. The walk-away trigger is therefore absent.
- **No committed lock-in.** Section 17(a) keeps the licence perpetual while fees are paid.

Sub-elements short of preferred — 90 days rather than 30, and no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on convenience termination (the refund at p0128 is confined to Garman default) — remain recorded as observations, consistent with the playbook's instruction not to escalate minor gaps against preferred into deviations.
